Perianal abscess

One case had resolution after incision and drainage with combined antimicrobial photodynamic therapy and PBM. The contribution of PBM and its effect on recurrence are unknown.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

One case had resolution after incision and drainage with combined antimicrobial photodynamic therapy and PBM. The contribution of PBM and its effect on recurrence are unknown.

Summary of the Evidence

One human case report directly concerns perianal abscess and describes PBM given together with antimicrobial photodynamic therapy after incision and drainage. A separate rat publication studies anal fistula, a related but distinct condition, rather than abscess treatment. These are not two clinical studies of the same indication. No controlled human trial or in-vitro/ex-vivo study was identified.

Human and clinical evidence

In the reported case, signs and symptoms of infection and inflammation resolved within five days after incision and drainage followed by aPDT and PBM. At three months, no fistulous tract or perianal collection was reported. This is a favorable clinical course after combined care, but the case cannot determine whether PBM added to the effects of drainage, aPDT, or other care, and it cannot estimate recurrence or fistula risk across patients (Campos et al. 2021).

Animal evidence

The related rat fistula-in-ano experiment did not test treatment of an abscess. Low-level laser reduced the area of the remaining fistulous tract and lowered inflammatory infiltrate and vascular congestion, but no animal had complete tract closure. These outcomes support a possible local effect on tissue inflammation, not proof of abscess resolution or prevention of fistula in people (Dos Santos et al. 2021).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No direct cell-culture or ex-vivo study of PBM for perianal abscess was identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The abscess case record does not provide a complete, reproducible PBM dose description. It combined PBM with aPDT and standard incision and drainage, so its protocol cannot isolate the light component. The related fistula experiment used 660-nm red visible laser at 3.57 J/cm², but this animal parameter should not be presented as a tested abscess protocol. No dose comparison or PBM-only clinical arm is available.

Interpretation

The single case documents resolution after combined treatment and drainage, which is a positive observation for that patient. It does not establish that PBM hastened resolution or prevented a later fistula. The rat fistula findings are adjacent mechanistic evidence and do not change the very limited direct evidence for perianal abscess.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for adjunctive PBM after drainage of perianal abscess
Publications and records1 article

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

One case reported resolution after drainage plus antimicrobial photodynamic therapy and PBM, so the light contribution cannot be separated from surgery or the antimicrobial treatment. A rat fistula study is related but does not test abscess care and did not fully close any tract. A controlled postoperative study separating interventions and tracking recurrence would be needed.
